correctness.rationale: After unit-distance normalization, \(\mathcal F(M)\) is the zero-sum hyperplane with norm \(\|\mu\|=\frac12\sum|\mu_i|\), and its unit ball is the convex hull of the molecules \(u_{ij}=e_i-e_j\). For any norm-one operator, finite norm attainment gives a molecule whose image has positive and negative mass one; the four sign configurations of its two selected coordinates yield an indicator functional norming the molecule and evaluating the image with modulus at least one half. Thus every norm-one operator has numerical radius at least one half. The explicit three-coordinate cyclic operator in the package has norm one and numerical radius at most one half; for a general norming pair, convex decomposition forces every positive-weight molecule to be normed by the same functional, extending the molecule estimate. The two-point boundary is one-dimensional.
correctness.risk: The theorem is real and finite; complex and infinite equilateral free spaces are outside scope.

value.rationale: Finite equilateral metrics form the canonical homogeneous family, and the numerical index is a natural operator-geometric invariant. The theorem gives an exact dimension-independent value in every dimension above one, with a sharp two-point threshold and an explicit extremal operator. This is a reusable family theorem rather than a tiny-instance computation.
value.risk: The result does not address complex scalars or non-equilateral metrics.

final_claim: For every finite real equilateral metric space \(M\) with \(|M|\ge3\), the Lipschitz-free space has numerical index \(n(\mathcal F(M))=1/2\); the two-point case is one-dimensional and has numerical index \(1\).
limitations: Finite equilateral metrics and real scalars only.
The two-point case has numerical index one and is excluded from the constant one-half regime.
